Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement asked me to get a concrete hosted-API rate card and a short note on how you bill tokens across models. Two things we need to understand before a pilot:

1) Do you bill per "model token" (i.e., tokens as counted by the model's tokenizer) or do you normalize across models? For example, if we send the same English document to two different models that use sentencepiece vs BPE, can billed tokens differ materially?

2) For planning purposes: rough baseline pricing for 1M input+output tokens per month on your hosted API for a small production pilot (one mid-tier LLM and one higher-quality LLM). We care about per-token rates and any minimums or committed tiers.

We will be testing English and some CJK samples. Any notes on how tokenization differences affect cost for multilingual content would also be helpful.

Could you send a short explainer and the rate card — procurement needs this to scope the PoC.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Rate card + tokenization question

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we bill by the model-specific token counts (i.e., the tokens as produced by the model's tokenizer). That means the same raw text can produce different billed token counts depending on the model and its tokenizer (sentencepiece vs BPE etc.).

A few practical notes:
- Billing unit: billed_tokens = tokens counted by the active model's tokenizer. Our console and invoices show billed token totals per model, per request.
- Why counts differ: tokenization algorithms split text differently. For typical English prose, BPE-style tokenizers used by GPT-family models often yield slightly fewer tokens than sentencepiece in many cases; for some languages or domain tokens (URLs/code), counts can flip.
- Multilingual/CJK: token counts can be higher for CJK depending on tokenizer training (some tokenizers treat individual characters as tokens, others use subword units). We can provide sample tokenization counts across your corpus.

I'll attach a short FAQ and a pilot quote. Priyom — can you include an indicative per-1k-token price for the two model families and a pilot discount? Monica — please flag anything about enterprise minimums or required PO language.

Thanks,
Marcus
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Rate card + tokenization question

Emma — attaching a concise FAQ and a pilot quote workbook (see attachments). Highlights here in-line so procurement can copy: 

Baseline (hosted API, month-to-month) — per 1,000 billed tokens (USD):
- mid-tier family (open-mid / optimized): $0.60 per 1k billed tokens
- high-quality family (large/opt structured for instruction): $1.80 per 1k billed tokens

Notes:
- These prices are host-level list rates for pay-as-you-go. We charge on billed_tokens per the selected model tokenizer.
- For a 1M billed-token month: mid-tier ≈ $600; high-quality ≈ $1,800.
- Pilot discount: we can offer a 15% discount on the first 3 months for pilots < 5M billed tokens total (applies to list rates above).
- Volume tiers / committed discounts: available at 5M+ and 25M+ monthly commitments — we can discuss a custom reserved capacity quote if you expect sustained usage.

Tokenization delta examples (approximate, English prose):
- 1,000-word English article (~6,000-8,000 characters): BPE (GPT-like) ≈ 750–850 tokens; sentencepiece (depending on vocab) ≈ 820–960 tokens.
- Code / URLs: token counts vary a lot; some tokenizers split URLs into many small subword tokens.

Multilingual call-out: Japanese/Chinese samples often show higher billed tokens if the tokenizer splits characters; we recommend sending a 50–100 sample doc set and we will provide per-model token counts so you can forecast cost accurately.

Attachments: Redwood-Tokenization-FAQ.pdf (tokenization examples and a short script for local token counting), Redwood-Pilot-Quote.xlsx (line items and pilot discount).

If that looks ok, I can convert the pilot quote to a PO-ready invoice and loop in Support/Legal for a short PoC attachment.

— Priyom

Subject: Re: Rate card + tokenization question

Mark — good questions. Short answers:
- Whitespace & normalization: our provided token-counting script mirrors the model tokenizer rules (normalization, whitespace handling) used at serving time. That means counts should match billed_tokens on the invoice for requests routed to that model.
- CJK: tokenizers differ. Some tokenizers trained on CJK languages use character-level tokens which can increase counts; sentencepiece models trained on multilingual corpora can be more compact in certain cases. We will run your provided samples through a short harness and return per-model billed token counts so you can see concrete deltas.
- Embeddings: billed by tokens for many embeddings endpoints; however, some of our embedding models have different per-1k-token prices (usually lower per token than high-quality generation models). The pilot quote workbook includes an embeddings line item (embeddings list: $0.20 per 1k billed tokens at list).

Action items:
1) Emma — please send a 50–100 doc sample (English + a few CJK samples). We will run tokenizers for the models in scope and return a short CSV with counts.
2) Procurement — if you want the PO template now we can prepare a 30-day pilot invoice that reflects the 15% discount and the two model lines.

Happy to set a 30-minute technical sync if your eng team wants to walk through the tokenization artifacts.

Best,
Marcus
